main_text.p: dio punctum est, à quo omnes lineæ ad superfici-em protensæ inter se sunt æquales. Punctum illud sphæræ centrum dicitur.
Dimidia sphæra ἡμισφαίριον medietate globi & maximo sphæræ circulo continetur.
Axis sphæræ linea recta est, circa quam sixam dimidius circulus circumactus sphæram describit.

Orbis distinguitur in solidum & cauum. Soli-dus idem est cum globo & sphæra. Cauus differt, duabus .n finitur superficiebus, conuexa exterio-re, concaua interiore. Sunt autem stellarum omni-um sixarum & errantium orbes caui non solidi.

A naturali sphæra differt Materialis, quam Græci uocant ἡρικοτὸν ἀπὸ τοῖς ἡρικοῖς, id est, ab armillis, Latini artificialem & armillarem & pertusam. Est enim materialis sphæra, quæ ex ar-millis seu circulis construitur, eo modo & coapta-tis

page.notes: The illustration is a woodcut of a hemisphere on two pillars, with reference letters α and γ; not transcribed as text. Greek words in the text are approximate: "ἡμισφαίριον" and "ἡρικοτὸν ἀπὸ τοῖς ἡρικοῖς" were not read letter by letter with certainty. Printed marks such as "a" and "y" near the woodcut are reference letters only. Page number absent; the watermark-like website URL at the foot is a digitiser's banner and was omitted.
